candidates.question: A personal project you chose has been sitting unfinished for several weeks. What would most naturally draw you back into it?

options.label: Choosing the next visible milestone and deciding to finish it
Finding a fresh angle that makes the project interesting again
Remembering the commitment I made and who it matters to
Working out why progress stopped and creating a more reliable approach

candidates.what_it_measures: What motive naturally restores follow-through after a self-chosen project loses momentum: completion, renewed interest, meaningful commitment, or a reliable method.
candidates.why_it_earns_a_place: It adds ordinary-life recovery evidence without asking whether the respondent is responsible or productive; each option offers a credible route back into the project.

candidates.question: You are beginning a hobby that has several ways to learn it. Which starting point feels most natural?

options.label: Pick a concrete result I want to achieve and practice toward it
Try several techniques and follow whichever one captures my interest
Learn alongside someone so the experience and encouragement are shared
Understand the fundamentals and build skill in a logical sequence

candidates.what_it_measures: The motivation that organizes entry into voluntary learning: outcome, exploration, shared experience, or coherent understanding.
candidates.why_it_earns_a_place: Learning entry is one of the thinnest audited domains, and the item avoids claiming that any color has a superior learning style.

candidates.question: You are choosing a household item that you will use often, and several options would work. What guides your choice most?

options.label: Which option solves the main need most directly
Which option offers the most enjoyable or flexible experience
Which option best fits the people and routines it will support
Which option has the strongest evidence of dependable long-term value

candidates.what_it_measures: The priority accepted when adequate purchase choices compete: direct utility, experience, household continuity, or verified value.
candidates.why_it_earns_a_place: It introduces a common purchasing context and a real accuracy tradeoff without making research the obviously intelligent response.

candidates.question: A family tradition still matters, but its old format no longer fits everyone’s lives. What matters most as you help shape its next version?

options.label: Choose a workable version that keeps the tradition happening
Give it a new form that people will be excited to experience
Preserve the sense of connection and meaning people rely on
Create a clear format and schedule that can hold up over time

candidates.what_it_measures: How continuity is protected when form can change: ongoing action, renewed experience, relational meaning, or sustainable structure.
candidates.why_it_earns_a_place: It measures stability and continuity through a family tradition rather than another sudden-disruption scenario.

candidates.question: At a gathering where you know almost no one, what kind of interaction are you most naturally drawn toward?

options.label: A focused conversation that leads to a useful idea or next step
Several lively conversations that open up new people and possibilities
A comfortable conversation where mutual trust can begin
A thoughtful conversation where we explore a subject in depth

candidates.what_it_measures: What a person seeks through communication with unfamiliar people: purposeful value, social energy, relational connection, or substantive understanding.
candidates.why_it_earns_a_place: It could replace generic sociability evidence with a motive-based unfamiliar-social discriminator while avoiding quietness as Yellow or Green evidence.

candidates.question: A favorite recipe keeps turning out differently even though each version is usable. What would you be most interested in trying next?

options.label: Choose the result I want and change the factor most likely to improve it
Experiment with a new variation and see what enjoyable result emerges
Adapt it around the tastes and experience of the people sharing it
Change one factor at a time so I can understand what produces each result

candidates.what_it_measures: The preferred way to frame an ordinary inconsistent outcome: target improvement, exploratory variation, shared experience, or causal understanding.
candidates.why_it_earns_a_place: It adds concrete everyday problem framing in a hobby context without asking who is the most competent cook or duplicating household-routine governance.

candidates.question: You have one open day in a place you have wanted to visit. How would you most naturally shape the day?

options.label: Choose the experience that matters most and build the day around completing it
Keep plenty of room to follow whatever looks interesting once I am there
Shape the day around a pace and experiences everyone can enjoy together
Research the route, timing, and key details so the day works smoothly

candidates.what_it_measures: The motive that anchors ordinary leisure planning: priority accomplishment, openness, shared experience, or dependable coherence.
candidates.why_it_earns_a_place: It adds travel planning without using disruption, emergency, or generic adaptability architecture.

candidates.question: A friend is choosing between two good opportunities and asks you to talk it through. Which question are you most naturally inclined to explore?

options.label: Which opportunity moves you closer to the result you want most?
Which opportunity opens the experiences and possibilities that energize you?
Which opportunity best fits the relationships and commitments you want to maintain?
Which opportunity holds up best when you compare the evidence and consequences?

candidates.what_it_measures: The lens naturally used to frame an underdetermined personal decision: outcome, possibility, commitments, or evidence.
candidates.why_it_earns_a_place: It measures problem framing through the question selected, not through giving competent advice or solving an urgent problem.

candidates.question: You join a casual activity that people enjoy in very different ways. Which part is most likely to keep you coming back?

options.label: Having a clear challenge and seeing myself improve
The energy, variety, and memorable moments around the activity
The dependable connection that develops with the people involved
Understanding the patterns and becoming more consistent over time

candidates.what_it_measures: What makes repeat recreation rewarding: achievement, experience, durable belonging, or mastery through understanding.
candidates.why_it_earns_a_place: It moves achievement evidence into recreation and gives every color an equally legitimate reason to return.

candidates.question: You and a sibling remember an important family event differently, but no practical decision depends on agreeing. What would you most naturally want from the conversation?

options.label: A clear conclusion about the main point so the disagreement can close
A lively exchange that leaves room for both versions of the story
Understanding how each version connects to what matters to each of us
Clarity about what can be verified and what genuinely remains uncertain

candidates.what_it_measures: What a person seeks from low-stakes disagreement when action is unnecessary: closure, expressive openness, relational understanding, or evidentiary clarity.
candidates.why_it_earns_a_place: It tests conflict motive in a non-decision family setting and keeps all four outcomes legitimate without making Yellow uniquely mature.

candidates.question: You are choosing one activity to make part of your regular week. What makes an option most appealing?

options.label: It gives me a clear goal and visible progress to pursue
It keeps bringing new experiences, people, or possibilities
It offers a dependable community where relationships can deepen
It offers a structured path for developing real understanding or skill

candidates.what_it_measures: What makes a recurring personal commitment attractive: progress, variety, belonging, or structured mastery.
candidates.why_it_earns_a_place: It deliberately tests the same broad motives in a forward-looking commitment choice rather than a learning start or retrospective recreation reward.

candidates.question: Someone asks for your opinion about something you know only partly. What response feels most natural?

options.label: Give the clearest useful recommendation I can and state the main limitation
Share the possibilities that seem most interesting and invite them to explore
Ask what matters to them so the opinion fits their situation
Check the important facts before offering a firm recommendation

candidates.what_it_measures: What a person protects when communicating under incomplete knowledge: usefulness, possibility, personal fit, or evidentiary confidence.
candidates.why_it_earns_a_place: It creates a balanced everyday accuracy tradeoff rather than asking whether the respondent is careful, honest, or helpful.

candidates.question: When a personal goal stops feeling exciting, I would rather keep working toward the result I chose than replace it with a more interesting goal.
candidates.what_it_measures: Red result commitment after novelty fades, balanced against the reasonable choice to redirect energy toward a more engaging goal.
candidates.why_it_earns_a_place: It gives the follow-through gap a direct Red-versus-Blue tradeoff without presenting persistence as universally virtuous.

candidates.question: When I discover something I enjoy, my first impulse is usually to invite others into the experience rather than keep exploring it on my own.
candidates.what_it_measures: Blue preference to expand personal enjoyment into shared expression and experience, rather than generic friendliness or social skill.
candidates.why_it_earns_a_place: It can replace generic sociability language with a motive-linked expression/experience tradeoff.

candidates.question: When deciding whether to leave a familiar group for a more appealing opportunity, I give more weight to the relationships I have built than to what the new experience might offer.
candidates.what_it_measures: Yellow preference for loyalty and durable belonging when it competes with an attractive new experience.
candidates.why_it_earns_a_place: It directly measures continuity and loyalty through a legitimate stay-versus-explore tradeoff without implying that either choice is more caring.

candidates.question: For a personal trip, I would rather settle the route and key details early than preserve maximum freedom to decide as I go.
candidates.what_it_measures: Green preference for predictable coherence when it directly competes with Blue freedom and spontaneity.
candidates.why_it_earns_a_place: It supplies a clean non-work planning tradeoff and deliberately parallels the travel scenario in a different response format.

pre_review_rejections.summary: A delayed trip forces a new plan.
pre_review_rejections.basis: Duplicates the disruption architecture already present in C01-S-03, C02-S-03, and C02-S-08.

pre_review_rejections.summary: Friends cannot agree on a restaurant.
pre_review_rejections.basis: Duplicates the stalled group-choice architecture in C01-S-07 and C02-S-15.
Duplicates incomplete-instruction and evidence-before-action content already represented by active questions and C01-L-G-01.
